lines.trans: Four golden cakes out of the oven without a single cracked top, Chef!
Feel this gentle shaded breeze under the tree—nature built us a cooling fan!
The whole courtyard smells like roasted almonds, ripe berries, and sweet summer sun!
Touch the side of tin one lightly, Ziad—is it warm rather than piping hot?
Just warm to the palm, Salma—ready for the thirty-year secret glaze!
Here is the warm honey whisked with sweet orange zest and two pastry brushes!
Brush gently from the centre outward so every berry shines like polished ruby glass.
And Nour scatters the toasted almond flakes right across the golden top!
Look at our twenty-eight birch clothespins holding every white napkin steady on the tables!
Wait—what time does the courtyard clock say right now, Ziad?
Twenty-eight minutes past two! My brother and I should walk to Central Station now!
Apron off, Ziad—I drew a brass compass welcome sign for you at the gate!

Goodbye!

meanings.note: Color adjective with feminine بيضا (beida) and plural بيض (biid).

examples.trans: We brought clean white sheets.
The gift is wrapped in white paper.

meanings.note: Takes a long -uu-/-oo- stem with possessive endings in Jordanian (أخوي my brother, أخوك your brother); dual أخوين.

examples.trans: My older brother lives in Amman.
The brothers sat together in the courtyard.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite noun أول means 'first' (أول يوم 'first day'); after a definite noun الأول / الأولى agrees in gender (الصفحة الأولى 'the first page'). Also used adverbially ('first').

examples.trans: Welcome on your first day of work!
Read the first page calmly.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of برتقال (collective noun; unit noun بردقانة 'one orange').

examples.trans: Fresh orange juice is nicest in the morning.

examples.text: جيب معك كيلو بردقان من السوق.
examples.trans: Bring a kilo of oranges with you from the market.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of برش ('to grate'). Used in baking for citrus zest (برش البرتقال 'orange zest', برش الليمون 'lemon zest').

examples.text: برش البرتقال بيعطي الكيكة ريحة حلوة.
examples.trans: Orange zest gives the cake a lovely aroma.
We added one teaspoon of lemon zest.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.
The taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Used for navigation or metaphorically for direction.

examples.trans: The brass compass always stays at the front desk.

examples.text: رسمنا بوصلة صغيرة على بطاقة الترحيب.
examples.trans: We drew a small compass on the welcome card.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of برّد (to cool down).

examples.text: حط الصينية على شبك التبريد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Put the tin on the cooling rack for ten minutes.
The cooling room keeps the fruit fresh.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رحّب (to welcome), central to Jordanian hospitality.

examples.trans: The hosts received us with a big welcome.
A short word of welcome makes the guests happy.

meanings.note: The number 30.

examples.trans: They have given us thirty days in the letter.
The bill is thirty-eight dinars.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun for berries/mulberries (singulative توتة 'one berry').

examples.trans: The berry and almond cake turned out delicious!
We have an old mulberry tree in the neighbourhood.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Masculine noun meaning the physical side of an object or person (distinct from the preposition جنب 'beside').

examples.text: امسح جنب الصينية قبل ما تفوتها الفرن.
examples.trans: Wipe the side of the tin before you put it in the oven.

examples.text: قعدت على جنب الطريق أستنى الباص.
examples.trans: I sat on the side of the road waiting for the bus.

meanings.note: Everyday counting unit for rolls of bread, fruit, lemons, or pills (خدي حبة take a piece; ست حبات ليمون six lemons).

examples.trans: Take a bread roll while it is hot.
I have six lemons in the basket.

حرق.gloss: to burn; scald; be piping hot

meanings.en: to burn; scald; be piping hot
meanings.note: Form I transitive verb; in everyday speech بتحرق also describes food or pans that are scorching hot.

examples.trans: Careful, the coffee is still hot and will burn!
He forgot the bread in the oven and burnt the edges.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بحس, بيحس).

examples.text: نتمنى كل ضيف يحس بالراحة هون.
examples.trans: We hope every guest feels at home here.
I felt the warmth the moment I walked in.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from خفيف ('light'). With preposition بـ, بخفة means 'lightly' or 'gently'.

examples.text: حرك السكر بخفة عشان ما يطير.
examples.trans: Stir the sugar gently so it doesn't fly about.

examples.text: بيمشي بخفة كأنه ما في وزن.
examples.trans: He walks lightly as if there were no weight.

meanings.note: Feminine instance noun from خلط ('to mix'): a spice blend, pastry glaze, or sauce mix.

examples.trans: We prepared the sugar and lemon glaze for the cake.

examples.text: كل بيت عنده خلطة بهارات خاصة.
examples.trans: Every home has its own special spice blend.

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.
Wait one minute, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دهبية, plural: دهبيين).

examples.trans: The gold tin is on the top shelf.

examples.text: فوق الباب في رسمة مفتاح دهبي.
examples.trans: Above the door there is a painted golden key.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for painting walls, shutters, or wooden furniture (noun دهان 'paint').

examples.text: رح ندهن الشيش باللون الأخضر يوم التنين.
examples.trans: We are going to paint the shutters green on Monday.

examples.text: دهنا الكراسي الخشب وتركناها تنشف بالشمس.
examples.trans: We painted the wooden chairs and left them to dry in the sun.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for drawing a picture, a map or a plan.

examples.trans: He drew me a map to the shop on a piece of paper.

examples.text: بنتي بترسم بيوت وشجر كل يوم.
examples.trans: My daughter draws houses and trees every day.

meanings.note: Geminate verb used for splashing water or sprinkling herbs/sugar.

examples.trans: I sprinkled a little water on the flowers in the morning.

examples.text: سلمى رشت قرفة مطحونة فوق الكيكة.
examples.trans: Salma dusted ground cinnamon over the cake.

meanings.note: Feminine noun from رقيق ('thin'). Broken plural رقائق refers to flakes (such as toasted almond flakes) or thin wafers.

examples.trans: We sprinkled toasted almond flakes on top.

examples.text: رقاقة العجين لازم تكون رفيعة كتير.
examples.trans: The dough sheet has to be very thin.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: روايح.

examples.trans: The aroma of coffee in the morning is wonderful!
The scent of cinnamon reaches the second floor.

meanings.note: Extremely common Levantine preposition meaning 'like' or 'similar to'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.
We sat drinking tea in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for an hour of time, a wristwatch, or a wall clock.

examples.trans: What time is it right now, please?
We arrived an hour ago on the dot.

meanings.note: From سر, a secret. A secret room is غرفة سرية.

examples.trans: I have a secret plan for the holiday.

examples.text: هاد الرقم سري، لا تحكيه لحدا.
examples.trans: This number is secret, do not tell anyone.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a tree.

examples.text: قطفنا ليمون أصفر طازة من شجرة الساحة.
examples.trans: We picked fresh yellow lemons from the courtyard tree.

examples.text: ظل الشجرة بيبرد القعدة وقت الظهر.
examples.trans: The shade of the tree cools the seating area at noon.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشلح, بيشلح).

examples.trans: Take off your heavy coat and sit down.
He took off his wet shoes by the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun in Arabic despite no -a ending.

examples.trans: The warm sun came out after the rain.
Read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Masculine geminate noun with broken plural شقوق ('cracks'), distinct from the verb شق ('to split').

examples.text: في شق صغير عالحيط جنب الشباك.
examples.trans: There is a small crack on the wall beside the window.

examples.text: لو ما فيها شقوق، الكيكة طلعت ممتازة.
examples.trans: If it has no cracks, the cake came out excellent.

meanings.note: The season of summer.

examples.trans: Evenings in Amman are pleasant in summer.
Our rent is paid until next summer.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: In تصرفي بطبيعتك, means 'act like your normal self / act naturally'.

examples.trans: Just be yourself.
Nature is lovely in spring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: Here is mint tea with honey.
Mountain honey tastes wonderful.

meanings.note: Extremely common colloquial conjunction used to indicate reason or purpose.

examples.trans: That is why the suitcase was heavy!
Are you polishing the lanterns for noon?

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعمل, بيعمل).

examples.text: اليوم رح نعمل بيض عالطريقة الفرنسية!
examples.trans: Today we will make French-style eggs!
What do we do now with the rain coming down?

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine word for a paintbrush, hairbrush, or pastry brush.

examples.text: غسلنا الفرشايات بمي دافية أول ما خلصنا دهان.
examples.trans: We washed the brushes in warm water right after finishing the painting.

examples.text: لا ترفع الإيد اللي ماسكة الفرشاية الخضرا!
examples.trans: Don't lift the hand that's holding the green paintbrush!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أفران.

examples.text: لفائف القرفة طلعت من الفرن هلا.
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven.
The bakery down the street bakes in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فوط.

examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water.
She wiped the table with a damp cloth.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Colloquial Levantine noun for cooling shade under a tree or awning (distinct from the particle/preposition في).

examples.trans: Sit in the shade under the mulberry tree.
The shade in the garden refreshes the spirit in summer.

meanings.note: Traditionally feminine noun with broken plural كفوف ('palms; gloves'). Used in baking to measure a light palm touch.

examples.trans: Test the warmth of the tin with the back of your palm.

examples.text: لبست كفوف المطبخ قبل ما تمسك الصينية.
examples.trans: She put on kitchen gloves before picking up the tin.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: In questions كم + singular noun asks 'how many?'; in statements كم + singular noun means 'a few' (كم دقيقة 'a few minutes').

examples.trans: Give him a few minutes, Rami.

examples.text: كم لفة قرفة بيقدر فرنك يخبز؟
examples.trans: How many cinnamon rolls can your oven bake?

meanings.note: Refers to a single, whole cake, or a distinct slice (singulative form of kēk).

examples.text: كيكة الليمون الصفرا طلعت من الفرن.
examples.trans: The yellow lemon cake came out of the oven.
We sliced the cake into six equal pieces.

meanings.note: Invariant modal word followed by a subjunctive verb (without ب-) to express 'must / have to / need to'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everything has to be just right!

meanings.note: Very common Jordanian word to indicate that an action is ongoing or hasn't happened yet.

examples.trans: Is your cup still intact?
Nobody has written anything yet.

meanings.note: Also used in the mild Jordanian exclamation يا لطيف! ('goodness gracious!').

examples.trans: Hot bread makes people pleasant!
Goodness gracious, the suitcase is so heavy!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلمس, بيلمس).

examples.trans: Touch the radiator — it is warm on top.
Touch the brass pipe — it heated up!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Vocalized in the dictionary to distinguish Form I intransitive لَمَع ('to shine') from Form II لمّع ('to polish').

examples.text: القزاز النظيف عم يلمع بشمس الصبح.
examples.trans: The clean glass is shining in the morning sun.

examples.text: خشب البيانو بيلمع تحت الضو الدافي.
examples.trans: The piano wood gleams under the warm light.

meanings.note: Active participle indicating the ongoing state of gripping or grasping something.

examples.trans: I am holding the torch steady!
He was holding a blue suitcase in his hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: محطات.

examples.trans: I arrived at the bus station in the morning.
The hotel is close to the station.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle from حمّص ('to toast/roast'): describes nuts, coffee, or bread.

examples.trans: Toasted walnuts give a nice crunch.

examples.text: شوية لوز محمص فوق الرز كتير زاكي.
examples.trans: A few toasted almonds on top of the rice are delicious.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from خفق ('to whisk'): describes beaten egg whites, cream, or batters.

examples.text: أضف البيض المخفوق شوي شوي عالخليط.
examples.trans: Add the beaten eggs little by little to the mixture.
Whipped cream is light and smooth.

meanings.note: Relative adjective from مركز ('centre'): used in المحطة المركزية ('Central Station') and السوق المركزي.

examples.trans: Let's meet at the Central Station entrance.
The central market is always full of activity.

meanings.note: Electric fan or hand fan (from ريح 'wind/breeze').

examples.text: شغلنا المروحة بالممر عشان ينشف الدهان أسرع.
examples.trans: We turned on the fan in the hallway so the paint would dry faster.

examples.text: هوا المروحة الخفيف حرك ريحة الدهان لبرا.
examples.trans: The gentle breeze from the fan carried the paint smell outside.

meanings.note: Masculine Levantine noun (plural مراييل) worn while cooking, painting, or crafting.

examples.text: البس مريول الرسم قبل ما تفتح الألوان.
examples.trans: Put on the painting apron before you open the paints.
The apron got splashed all over with blue ink.

meanings.note: Form VIII participle from root س-و-ي. Means level/flat for surfaces, and 'well-cooked/ripe' for food.

examples.trans: Put it on a level surface.
The table isn't level, it wobbles.

meanings.note: Common defective verb for walking on foot or things running smoothly.

examples.text: ممنوع تمشي عكاحلك لحد بكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: You mustn't walk on your ankle until tomorrow morning.

examples.text: مشينا عالهدا بالساحة بعد ما وقفت المطر.
examples.trans: We walked gently across the courtyard after the rain stopped.

meanings.note: Form I passive participle from صقل ('to polish'): describes glossy tile, stone, or glazed surfaces.

examples.trans: The hall tile is polished and gleaming.

examples.text: النحاس المصقول بيعكس الضو متل المراية.
examples.trans: Polished brass reflects the light like a mirror.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Everyday Arabic bakery noun for pastries and baked doughs.

examples.trans: We made a tray of fresh pastries for breakfast.
The pastries are still hot from the oven.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Fine tweezers for delicate repair work, or small kitchen tongs.

examples.text: طارق طلب ملقط رفيع عشان يمسك الدبوس النحاس.
examples.trans: Tariq asked for thin tweezers to hold the tiny brass pin.

examples.text: البرغي الصغير ما بينمسك إلا بملقط.
examples.trans: That tiny screw can only be picked up with tweezers.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural نسمات / أنسام) for a pleasant light breeze, especially in the evening.

examples.text: في نسيم بارد لطيف عالسطح بالليل.
examples.trans: There is a pleasant cool breeze on the roof at night.
The sea breeze moved the lanterns gently.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Lively conversational exclamation of triumph or attention ('ha! / there!').

examples.text: ما صاب قميصي ولا نقطة دهان، ها!
examples.trans: Not a single drop of paint touched my shirt—ha!

examples.text: ها، شو رأيكم باللون الأخضر تحت الشمس؟
examples.trans: Well, what do you think of the green colour in the sunshine?

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; وجه لوجه means 'face to face'. Plural: وجوه.

examples.trans: They stood face to face under the tree.
The top of the cake turned golden in the oven.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Collective masculine noun (unit noun ياقوتة 'one ruby'). Used metaphorically for deep ruby-red colour in berries or glaze.

examples.trans: The colour of the red berries is like ruby.

examples.text: عندها خاتم فضة عليه حجر ياقوت.
examples.trans: She has a silver ring with a ruby stone on it.
